newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan shares maintain modest recovery.
newsitem.headline: Jordan shares maintain modest recovery.

text.p: Shares on the Jordanian stock exchange maintained Wednesday's modest recovery at the start of weekly trade on Saturday, rising 0.33 percent in quiet trade boosted by investor interest in a few leading shares.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose 0.48 points to 147.24 points in trade worth 400,000 dinars ($565,000).
Brokers said Jordan Gulf Bank led the way with a 0.03 dinar rise to 0.95 dinars in trade worth 85,000 dinars. Arab Bank rose 1.50 dinars to 247 dinars in turnover of 34,000 dinars.
"There's been some outside buying in the banks, but otherwise the trend is still weak," said one broker.
International Tobacco and Livestock and Poultry also rose in relatively busy trade.
Overall rising stocks outnumbered by 18 to 12, with shares in another 11 companies trading but closing unchanged.
Last Tuesday the AFM index fell to 146.34 points, its lowest level since early September.

Turnover, blighted by domestic economic worries and fears that Jordan will continue to be blocked out of trade with the neighbouring West Bank and sanction-hit Iraq, has halved since September to around 500,000 dinars a day.
